transcript:
[doctor] Hi Ms. Lee, how are you today?

[patient] Hi, I'm okay, but I've been having some pain in my shoulder that's really bothering me.

[doctor] I'm sorry to hear that. Can you tell me more about the pain in your shoulder?

[patient] Sure. It's been hurting for about a month now, especially when I lift or reach for something. Sometimes it even radiates down to my hand and causes a tingling sensation.

[doctor] I see. Is the pain constant or does it come and go?

[patient] It's mostly there all the time, but it definitely gets worse with certain movements.

[doctor] Alright. How would you rate the severity of your pain on a scale from 1 to 10, with 10 being the worst pain imaginable?

[patient] I'd say it's around a 6 or 7 most of the time.

[doctor] Hmm, that sounds quite uncomfortable. Has this pain affected your daily activities or work?

[patient] Yes, I'm a graphic designer, and it's been really hard to do my job. I also can't exercise like I used to, and it's even hard to fall asleep because of the pain.

[doctor] That must be very frustrating. Have you noticed any other symptoms, such as numbness or weakness in your arm or hand?

[patient] No numbness or weakness, just the occasional tingling in my right hand.

[doctor] Okay. Have you tried any treatments or medications to relieve the pain?

[patient] I've tried some over-the-counter pain relievers like ibuprofen, but they don't seem to help much.

[doctor] Alright. I understand from your records that you have a history of depression. How are you managing that currently?

[patient] I'm on medication for it, but the pain is making things worse. It's hard to stay positive when I'm in pain all the time.

[doctor] I can see how that would be challenging. We'll work on addressing your shoulder pain to help improve your overall well-being. Let's start with a physical exam.

[doctor] I'm going to inspect your shoulder first. I don't see any visible deformity or swelling. Now, I'll palpate the area. Does it hurt when I press here on your biceps tendon?

[patient] Yes, that's tender.

[doctor] Alright. Let's check your range of motion. Can you try to rotate your shoulder externally?

[patient] It's a bit painful and feels limited.

[doctor] I see. Now, I'm going to perform a special test called Speed’s test to check for biceps tendinitis. Please resist as I push down on your arm. Does this cause pain?

[patient] Yes, that hurts quite a bit.

[doctor] Thank you for that. Based on the examination, it seems likely that you have biceps tendinitis. We'll await the X-ray results to rule out any structural abnormalities. 

[doctor] Your vital signs are all within normal ranges. Your blood pressure is 118/76 mmHg, heart rate is 72 bpm, respiratory rate is 16 breaths per minute, and your temperature is 98.6°F.

[patient] That's good to hear.

[doctor] For your shoulder pain, I'm going to prescribe Cyclobenzaprine 10 mg, to be taken orally three times daily for 7 days. Here are 21 tablets for that. I'm also prescribing Acetaminophen 500 mg, to be taken every 6 hours as needed for pain. You will have 30 tablets of that.

[patient] Thank you. I hope that helps.

[doctor] We will also need to get an X-ray of your right shoulder to check for any structural issues. I've already ordered that, so we should have the results soon.

[patient] Alright, I'll get that done.

[doctor] In the meantime, let's talk about some lifestyle recommendations. It's important to incorporate a balanced diet with more vegetables to improve your overall health. 

[patient] I can definitely try to do that.

[doctor] Also, I suggest starting a gentle exercise program focusing on shoulder stretches and strengthening exercises as tolerated. This should help with your mobility and pain.

[patient] Okay, I'll give that a try.

[doctor] Given your history of depression, it might also be helpful to seek support for your depressive symptoms. We can consider adjusting your current treatment for depression if the combination of pain and mental health is significantly affecting you.

[patient] Yes, that sounds like a good idea.

[doctor] Make sure to use proper body mechanics at work to avoid further strain on your shoulder. This includes adjusting your workstation to ensure it's ergonomically friendly.

[patient] I'll look into that. 

[doctor] Lastly, it's crucial to adhere to the prescribed medication regimen and follow up on the imaging results. We will discuss any additional testing if required based on those results.

[patient] I understand. I'll make sure to follow the instructions.

[doctor] Great. We've scheduled a follow-up appointment in 4 weeks to assess your improvement and discuss alternative treatments if necessary. Does that work for you?

[patient] Yes, that works for me.

[doctor] Perfect. Do you have any other questions or concerns?

[patient] No, I think you've covered everything. Thank you.

[doctor] You're welcome, Ms. Lee. I'm confident that with these steps, we can help alleviate your pain and improve your overall well-being. Take care and see you in 4 weeks.

[patient] Thank you, doctor. I appreciate your help.

[doctor] You're welcome. Goodbye.
